clue.text: Fancy finding green around the gills in fish

indicators.note: one thing placed around another wraps it, so the fish encloses the sickly word

parts.note: fry are young fish
looking green around the gills means feeling sick

explanation.surface: An angler admires a fancy-looking fish that seems a bit green around the gills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green around the gills' reads as a description of the fish, but it is the phrase for sickness, which sits inside the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Frilly clothing is decorated with ruffles, so it is ornate or fancy rather than plain.

clue.text: Dance round tree, indecently exposed

indicators.note: going round something encircles it, so the dance word surrounds the tree

parts.note: a fling is a lively Scottish dance, as in the Highland fling
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: Someone dancing round a maypole has been caught showing too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Flashing is slang for briefly and indecently showing one's private parts in public.

clue.text: Rude little devil, Eliot, unfortunately

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous demon

indicators.note: something that goes unfortunately goes awry, so the poet's letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A literary insult: the poet Eliot was, sadly, a rude little devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Impolite means lacking good manners, which is a standard synonym of rude.

clue.text: Nest where I fed tailless bird

indicators.note: food that is fed goes inside, so the bird takes in the letter
without a tail means the last letter of the bird is cut off

parts.note: the lark is a songbird
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recalls feeding a bird with no tail in its nest.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the K from the bird first, then put I inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is an animal's den or resting place, much as a nest is a creature's home.

clue.text: One recently gone into earth o the beaten path

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: something that has gone into a thing sits inside it, so the earth wraps the departed word

parts.note: sod is a piece of turf or earth
late can mean recently deceased or recently past

explanation.surface: A funeral note: someone who recently died has been buried in earth far from the beaten track.
explanation.walkthrough: The source prints 'o' for 'off'. 'Recently gone' reads as a death, and late is the word for the recently deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: A place off the beaten path is remote and far from others, which is what isolated means.

clue.text: Number joining party, meal made?

definitions.note: the question mark asks for the fuss itself, as in making a meal of something

parts.note: a number is a piece of music in a show
and is the word that joins things
a dance is a social party with music

explanation.surface: A guest joins a party and is served a proper dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: To make a meal of something is to fuss over it, and so is making a song and dance about it; the question mark flags this indirect definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A song and dance is a fuss or an elaborate commotion, the same as the idiom of making a meal of things.

clue.text: Veg out, lots of lovely leeks, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the leading letter of each word counts

parts.note: the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Relax with plenty of nice leeks — a pun on 'veg' as vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Veg out' suggests vegetables, chiming with the leeks, but it means to laze about.
explanation.definitionFit: To loll is to lounge lazily, sprawled and relaxed, which is what vegging out is.

clue.text: Model eating stew…

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashion model is tucking into a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like the diner; it is the signal to rework the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tagine is a slow-cooked North African stew, named after the conical clay pot it is made in.

clue.text: …stew in salmagundi, therefore

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: the stew is therefore a salmagundi, a mixed dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the stew in 7-down, but here stew is a verb: to fret anxiously.
explanation.definitionFit: To stew is to worry and be agitated, and to dither is to be in a nervous, indecisive state.

clue.text: Live–in babysitter in a cheerful mood

parts.note: taken as written
feeling up means in good spirits
an air is a manner or atmosphere, as in an air of gloom

explanation.surface: A babysitter who lives with the family is in good spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: An au pair is a young foreign helper who lives with a host family and looks after the children.

clue.text: Fin unusually weightless on a plane

indicators.note: something done unusually is done out of its normal order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
light means of little weight

explanation.surface: A Finn feels strangely weightless while flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fin' looks like a nationality or a fish part; it is just three letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in flight takes place while an aircraft is flying, such as in-flight meals served on a plane.

clue.text: One's gran, real drunken lady who lunches

indicators.note: drunken suggests reeling and lurching about, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's grandmother turns out to be a tipsy society lunch-goer.
explanation.walkthrough: A Sloane Ranger is a well-off, upper-class young Londoner, named after Sloane Square in Chelsea.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady who lunches is a wealthy woman of leisure, and the Sloane Ranger is the British upper-class stereotype of one.

clue.text: Small beer imbibed by Neanderthal fellow

indicators.note: something imbibed is taken inside, so the answer is swallowed within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A caveman knocks back a modest drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small beer' usually means something trivial; here it is literal, a half-pint ordered at a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: In a British pub a half is a half-pint glass of beer, the smaller measure.

clue.text: Maestro with large pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so these letters are poor as they stand and must be reorganised

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A conductor appears in a pair of oversized trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like a noun for underwear; in British slang it means rubbish, which signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Elgar was an English composer, a master of music and so a maestro.

clue.text: Joint in between kids passed around

indicators.note: passed around suggests turning back the other way, so the run of letters is read from right to left
in says the answer is lodged inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A cannabis joint is handed round among a group of youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests a smoke passed round by the kids, but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge joint in the middle of the leg.

clue.text: Old Dutch saves kiss for dog

indicators.note: to save something is to hold onto it, so the Dutch word keeps the kiss inside

parts.note: the Boers were settlers of Dutch origin in South Africa
X is the written sign for a kiss

explanation.surface: An old Dutchman holds back a kiss meant for his dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Dutch' is also Cockney slang for a wife, which suits the kiss; here it is the settler.
explanation.definitionFit: The boxer is a breed of medium-sized, short-haired dog originally developed in Germany.

clue.text: Song sheet initially in hand

indicators.note: in places the chosen letter inside the following word

parts.note: the palm is the inner surface of the hand

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A singer holds a hymn sheet in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song or hymn, especially one from the Book of Psalms in the Bible.

clue.text: So in Thailand, when cooked — it's pad Thai!

indicators.note: cooked food is transformed from its raw state, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: In Thailand, the thing everyone cooks is pad Thai.
explanation.definitionFit: Pad Thai, stir-fried rice noodles, is widely regarded as Thailand's signature food, an example of a country's emblematic meal.

clue.text: Article in short that's OK

indicators.note: in places the article inside the phrase for short

parts.note: short means not tall
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An editor approves a piece of writing in brief form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' must be expanded to a two-word phrase before the article goes between the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'not at all' in reply to thanks is a polite way of saying it was no trouble, the same as 'that's OK'.

clue.text: Prize busybody, most porky

parts.note: a plum is a choice prize, as in a plum job
a pest is an annoying nuisance

explanation.surface: An award goes to the most overweight meddler.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump and porky both mean rather fat, so the superlative plumpest equals most porky.

clue.text: Kitchen liquid in goblet I leave out

indicators.note: out here means out of place or disordered, so these letters are put in another order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a drink behind in a goblet on the kitchen table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitchen liquid in goblet' sounds like a description; 'in' only joins the definition to the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegetable oil is a cooking fat kept in kitchens, pressed from plants and liquid at room temperature.

clue.text: Clear miss in evacuation of Germany

indicators.note: in places the young woman inside the remaining outer letters
evacuating a word empties out its middle, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A young woman is evacuated from Germany, leaving the way clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Glassy water is smooth and transparent, so it is clear like glass.

clue.text: Country located in Vietnam, on a corner

indicators.note: located in says the answer is found sitting inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across four words

explanation.surface: A place found in Vietnam, on a street corner.
explanation.definitionFit: Monaco is a tiny independent principality on the French Riviera, a sovereign state.

clue.text: Play instrument backwards

indicators.note: backwards tells us to read the word for an implement from its end to its start

parts.note: a tool is an instrument for doing a job

explanation.surface: A musician performs a piece in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play instrument' reads as making music; Play is the definition, a stage work.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot is a black comedy stage play by Joe Orton, first staged in 1965.

clue.text: Walk four weeks and three days

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to walk in step, like soldiers
second meaning: a 31-day month of the year

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a calendar sum: 28 plus 3 days makes 31, the length of the third month.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for walking with a measured military tread and the name of a month lasting 31 days.

clue.text: Royal title unchanged on reflection?

parts.note: surface reading: a monarch's title that stays the same after careful thought
setter's reading: a royal form of address that reads the same in a mirror, backwards as forwards

explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflection' suggests thinking, but it means mirroring: the title is a palindrome, the same read from either end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ma'am, rhyming with jam, is how a British queen is addressed after first being called Your Majesty.

clue.text: A jewel lifted, magnificent

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the letters runs them upward, so they read in the opposite order

parts.note: taken as written
a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A splendid gemstone has been stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifted' looks like slang for stolen, which suits a jewel; in a down clue it turns the letters upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is informal slang for excellent or huge, an enthusiastic word like magnificent.

clue.text: On holiday, a king of Mercia

parts.note: someone off work is on leave
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Anglo-Saxon king takes a vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in the English Midlands; its ruler built the earthwork called Offa's Dyke.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa ruled the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia in the eighth century and was its most powerful monarch.

clue.text: Futuristic health resort, people ultimately confined to prison

parts.note: a spa is a resort offering health treatments

indicators.note: something confined to a place is shut inside it, so the jail surrounds the chosen letter

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A modern spa where guests feel shut in like prisoners.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter goes inside the jail word just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Space-age design looks like it belongs to the era of space travel, so it is very modern or futuristic.

clue.text: Old residence back on sale recently

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
a flat is an apartment, a place to live

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, the only one kept here

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An old house has lately come back onto the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back on sale' reads as relisted; 'back' takes the last letter of sale, and 'on' places it after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Of late is an idiom meaning lately, in the recent past.

clue.text: One may fancy track for old farmers

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine freely, so these letters are reimagined in another order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A person might take a liking to a rural trail suited to old-time farmers.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeomanry were the class of small freehold farmers in historical England who worked their own land.

clue.text: Legate trained small bird

indicators.note: trained means shaped or drilled into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A papal envoy has taught a little bird some tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: An eaglet is a young eagle, a bird of prey not yet grown to full size.
